column2: A town armoury: a sturdy two-storey building with a grey dressed-stone ground floor and a half-timbered upper floor of cream plaster and dark oak, a steep red clay-tile roof with a stone chimney, a wide arched oak double door bound in iron, racks of spears and halberds and a row of round wooden shields painted red with a black eagle hung along the front wall, a suit of plate armour on a wooden stand beside the door, one red cloth banner with a black eagle hanging from an iron bracket.

A large farm barn: a long timber-framed barn with dark oak frame and plank walls over a low rough stone base, a tall steep golden straw thatch roof with a neat ridge, big double plank doors standing open on the long side showing hay inside, a small hay loft door under the gable with a hoist beam, a stack of hay bales and a wooden pitchfork leaning by the doors.

A village granary: a square timber-and-plank storehouse raised off the ground on short stone staddle stones (mushroom-shaped stone pillars) so rats cannot climb in, dark oak frame with plank walls, a steep golden straw thatch roof, a small plank door reached by a few wooden steps, plump tied burlap grain sacks stacked by the steps.

A small square livestock pen with no animals: a sturdy rustic split-rail wooden fence of weathered oak posts and rails enclosing a patch of trodden earth with a little straw, a simple plank gate on one side, a hollowed log feeding trough and a wooden water bucket inside, a small lean-to shelter of planks with a short red clay-tile roof in one corner.
